acceptance_criteria.criterion: Calling saveConfigField('gitCredentials', { 'github.com': 'token' }) writes the field to config.json while keeping all other fields intact.
Calling saveConfigField('gitCredentials', undefined) removes the field from config.json.
The _instructions field in config.json survives a write round-trip.
Unit tests in config.test.ts cover both the set and delete paths.

summary: Added saveConfigField(field, value, configPath?) to src/config/config.ts. Sets or deletes a top-level JSON field, preserving all other fields including _instructions.
Added writeJsonFile import to config.ts (was previously using only readJsonFile).
Added 5 unit tests in config.test.ts covering: set field, delete field, _instructions survival, overwrite, and no-op delete. All 22 config tests pass.

comments.note: config.ts: saveConfigField() accepts field as string rather than keyof AppConfig. This is intentional since callers may store non-typed fields (e.g. _instructions). If the API surface later needs to be restricted to known AppConfig keys, a function overload could be added.
No observations — code in saveConfigField() is clean, minimal, and consistent with existing module patterns.

summary: All 4 ACs verified via 5 dedicated saveConfigField tests (all already confirmed passing in the 22-test config suite). AC1: set + all other fields preserved including _instructions. AC2: delete removes the field, other fields intact. AC3: _instructions survives round-trip (explicit dedicated test). AC4: both set and delete paths covered. Full regression: 507/507 pass.

Reviewed saveConfigField() in config.ts and its 5 dedicated tests. No blocking issues. The function is minimal and correct: read-modify-write using the existing json-storage layer, unconditional field delete when value is undefined, all other fields preserved. The field: string parameter (no allowlist at function level) is the correct design for a low-level utility — call-site allowlisting is the appropriate control. No Fix-Forward changes needed.
